questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Career opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: English speaking country and a university with a very good reputation

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: The information needed was accesible and the people at McGill were very helpfull.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: There was a receptionist

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: McGill in general offered good assistance, however specifically the faculty of Law was lacking a bit. Many informations needed was not accesible.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: I lived in "on campus-housing" however it was not located at campus which was very nice while this did not include a mealplan, which I was not interested in.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: Most of the on campus housing options have a mandatory meal plan. Be aware of that

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: It is a great opportunity if you want to know other exchange students! However I think there is also something charming about not living on campus, but founding something yourself.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: While a big part of the faculty was on strike it was made very difficult. Furthermore I found it difficult to find information on the courses offered.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: It was online and easy enough

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: You can always write to the faculty but otherwise a lot of information was online

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Because of the faculty being on strike I was not able to register for the classes I originally wanted. I therefore ended up in some random courses.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Register in courses without a final exam but with only a final assignment. That was so nice!

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I thought the level on the courses was fine.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The style of teaching was very different. There was a lot of tests and assignments due during the semester which was very different compared to UCPH

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Banking Law
Family Property Law

Class Actions in the Quebec Regime

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: All kinds of!

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Friday bars:)

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Do some trips outside of Montreal

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Easy - Montreal is different than Copenhagen, but being a big city many things are also similar

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Go to events arranged by the university

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The french speaking! It was no issue because everyone speaks english, but I was surprised by how much french speaking there is

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Loved the wheather! And people are very friendly

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Be aware that there is a lot of tests and assignments during the semester
Be aware of the french speaking even though it is really no problem if you dont speak it

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: There is a lot of activities you can join however I did not find it necessary to join frosh week. During frosh week you hang out with first year students and therefore you will not have any classes with these people. It was to be a part of but I dont find it necessary and I ended up skipping the last part of the week to prioritize haning out with people who I knew I would have more interactions with during the semester.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Meeting new people and getting to know a new city and culture very well

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: homesickness :)

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Very good experience - do it :))

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
